rows: Removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Rights can be suspended during a National Emergency.
Articles 20 and 21 serve as crucial exceptions and cannot be suspended during an emergency.
The Right to Property was officially removed from Fundamental Rights via the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
The Right to Education was introduced as Article 21A through the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
Exams frequently test which articles remain active during an emergency: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under any circumstance.
Remember the year and amendment for Right to Property: 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
Article 21A (Right to Education) was added specifically by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

blocks.content:
44th Amendment Act, 1978 – Removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights.
86th Amendment Act, 2002 – Added Right to Education (Article 21A).
